title: AI Spending Is The Honey Badger Of Budgets
gist: Gartner forecasts AI spending of $1.79T in 2025 rising to $3.64T in 2027, overtaking shrinking traditional IT spending in 2027 on the author's estimates. Roughly $6.1T of AI capex by hyperscalers and model builders would consume nearly all of their roughly $6.2T of revenue, forcing debt and vendor financing.

insights.claim: Gartner puts AI spending at $1.79 trillion in 2025 (up 2.6X), $2.67 trillion in 2026 (up 49.7%) and $3.64 trillion in 2027 (up 36%).
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Sets the scale and decelerating-but-huge growth path for AI demand.

insights.claim: Gartner's forecasts for AI infrastructure spending (servers, storage, switching) keep being revised upward: 2025 rose from $975.6B to $981.9B, with +$52.9B added for 2026 and +$87.4B for 2027.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Estimates keep ratcheting up despite bubble worries, supporting continued supplier revenue.

insights.claim: The author suspects the upward revisions in AI infrastructure spending are largely from hyperscaler and cloud-builder XPU designs, used internally and sold to model builders like OpenAI and Anthropic, plus some incremental Nvidia and AMD GPU system sales.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Custom silicon is capturing a growing share of incremental AI capex relative to merchant GPUs.

insights.claim: AI spending is described as resilient to inflation, bubble worries, power constraints, supply chain problems and political instability, with forecasts only revised upward.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Forecast momentum has so far ignored macro and physical constraints.

insights.claim: Gartner now separates GenAI model licenses and AI agents and assistants from AI data science/ML platforms and AI development platforms, distinct from enterprise software with embedded AI.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Finer categories will let investors track where GenAI software revenue actually lands.
insights.locator: What is new with the latest

insights.claim: Traditional datacenter IT spending has been in recession since the 2023 GenAI boom and is expected to stay in recession for the foreseeable future.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: AI is displacing, not adding to, conventional IT budgets.
insights.locator: traditional datacenter IT spending is in recession

insights.claim: Traditional IT spending shrank 12.5% in 2025 to $3.79 trillion and is forecast to fall 2.5% in 2026 to $3.69 trillion and 9.5% in 2027 to $3.43 trillion.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Legacy server and enterprise IT vendors face structural shrinkage.

insights.claim: Total IT spending rose 10.7% to $5.58 trillion in 2025; the author estimates $6.98 trillion (up 9.6%) for 2027 because Gartner has not published a public 2027 total.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The author's own 2027 estimate drives the crossover claim, so it is soft.

insights.claim: On the author's estimates, 2027 is the first year AI spending ($3.64T) exceeds traditional IT spending ($3.43T).
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Marks a crossover where AI becomes the largest IT spending category.

insights.claim: AI is a new datacenter architecture that rivals the debut of commercial computing six decades ago, and the current cycle is called the most dramatic IT investment cycle in history.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Frames AI as a platform shift, not a cyclical blip.

themes.theme: Definitions: what counts as AI spend

insights.claim: The author excludes AI smartphones and AI PCs from AI infrastructure because AI features there are largely incidental to ordinary device purchases.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Headline AI totals depend on definitions; stricter counting shrinks the narrative.

insights.claim: The author thinks customers upgrade enterprise software for general reasons and get AI functionality bundled, so AI is just another function in the application stack and eventually just what software does.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Embedded-AI software spend may overstate direct demand for AI.
insights.locator: AI is just another set of functions

insights.claim: Hyperscaler, cloud and consumer-digital-service revenue (Google, Microsoft, AWS, Meta, ByteDance) totals roughly $6.2 trillion across 2025-2027 per Synergy Research, eyeballed from a chart.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Revenue base against which the AI capex must be judged.
insights.locator: If you add up the revenues

insights.claim: Assuming 75% of AI spending comes from hyperscalers, cloud builders and model builders, they would need about $6.1 trillion, nearly all of their revenue, to fund their AI infrastructure plans.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Capex plans exceed what operating cash flow can cover, implying heavy external financing.

insights.claim: The shortfall explains the turn to debt financing, vendor financing from Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom, and roundtripping deals.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Circular and vendor financing is a structural feature and a systemic risk in AI supply chains.
insights.locator: This is why the tech titans

insights.claim: Neoclouds, sovereign clouds and enterprises face the same funding issues to a lesser or equal degree, and AI must start removing costs to support further AI investment.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Smaller AI buyers are even more dependent on outside capital and on AI delivering savings.

insights.claim: Synergy's chart shows service-provider revenue streams more than doubling over 2028-2031, so the buildout is borrowing against a large future, and that borrowing is what could make the future happen.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The financing depends on a revenue doubling that is unproven.
insights.locator: the revenue streams are going to more than double

insights.claim: Synergy's John Dinsdale expects revenue growth among these providers from 2026 on to outpace 2020-2025.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Supports the revenue side of the AI capex justification.

insights.claim: Gartner's John-David Lovelock says the AI datacenter buildout is the largest infrastructure project humanity has undertaken, with AI-optimized servers bought by hyperscalers and service providers the largest single spending area.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Server spending by hyperscalers remains the key demand driver for chip and system vendors.
insights.locator: The buildout of AI data center
